question: Before a new main is placed in service, what is the main purpose of disinfecting it?
correctAnswer: To kill or inactivate bacteria introduced during construction
explanation: Disinfection destroys bacteria picked up from soil, handling, and trench water during installation, so the main does not contaminate the distribution system.
options: To kill or inactivate bacteria introduced during construction
To increase the pressure rating of the pipe
To remove all dissolved minerals from the water
To coat the pipe interior against corrosion
optionA: To kill or inactivate bacteria introduced during construction
optionB: To increase the pressure rating of the pipe
optionC: To remove all dissolved minerals from the water
optionD: To coat the pipe interior against corrosion
sourceReference: Supporting topic reference: Disinfection of New Mains. See README for source scope and limitations.

question: What step normally comes immediately before chlorinating a newly installed main?
correctAnswer: Flushing the main to remove dirt and debris
explanation: Flushing first removes sediment and construction debris, which would otherwise consume chlorine and shield bacteria from disinfection.
options: Connecting customer services to the main
Flushing the main to remove dirt and debris
Painting the hydrants on the new section
Lowering the system pressure to zero
optionA: Connecting customer services to the main
optionB: Flushing the main to remove dirt and debris
optionC: Painting the hydrants on the new section
optionD: Lowering the system pressure to zero
sourceReference: Supporting topic reference: Disinfection of New Mains. See README for source scope and limitations.

question: After disinfection and final flushing, what must be satisfactory before a new main is tied into the live system?
correctAnswer: Bacteriological test results from samples taken from the main
explanation: Satisfactory bacteriological results confirm the disinfection worked, so the main is cleared for connection only after those results are received.
options: A pressure test witnessed by every customer on the street
A full year of operating records for the new main
Bacteriological test results from samples taken from the main
A colour comparison against bottled water
optionA: A pressure test witnessed by every customer on the street
optionB: A full year of operating records for the new main
optionC: Bacteriological test results from samples taken from the main
optionD: A colour comparison against bottled water
sourceReference: Supporting topic reference: Disinfection of New Mains. See README for source scope and limitations.

question: Why is a new main filled slowly during the disinfection procedure?
correctAnswer: To let trapped air escape and avoid pressure surges
explanation: Slow filling lets air vent through hydrants or air valves, which prevents air binding and damaging pressure surges in the new pipe.
options: To give the chlorine more time to evaporate
To keep the pipe from floating in the trench permanently
To reduce the amount of water used to zero
To let trapped air escape and avoid pressure surges
optionA: To give the chlorine more time to evaporate
optionB: To keep the pipe from floating in the trench permanently
optionC: To reduce the amount of water used to zero
optionD: To let trapped air escape and avoid pressure surges
sourceReference: Supporting topic reference: Disinfection of New Mains. See README for source scope and limitations.

question: What is done with the heavily chlorinated water used to disinfect a new main?
correctAnswer: It is flushed out and disposed of safely, away from sensitive watercourses where required
explanation: Superchlorinated flush water is removed before service and handled so its high chlorine does not harm customers or the receiving environment.
options: It is delivered directly to customers as extra protection
It is flushed out and disposed of safely, away from sensitive watercourses where required
It is stored in the reservoir for later blending without testing
It is left in the main indefinitely
optionA: It is delivered directly to customers as extra protection
optionB: It is flushed out and disposed of safely, away from sensitive watercourses where required
optionC: It is stored in the reservoir for later blending without testing
optionD: It is left in the main indefinitely
sourceReference: Supporting topic reference: Disinfection of New Mains. See README for source scope and limitations.

question: What does a reddish brown discolouration at customer taps most commonly indicate in an older iron main area?
correctAnswer: Corrosion products and tuberculation being released from iron pipe
explanation: Iron corrosion forms rust coloured deposits inside the pipe, and flow changes can release them as red water at taps.
options: Excess chlorine forming a red dye in the water
Algae growing inside the household plumbing only
Corrosion products and tuberculation being released from iron pipe
A failure of the water meter register
optionA: Excess chlorine forming a red dye in the water
optionB: Algae growing inside the household plumbing only
optionC: Corrosion products and tuberculation being released from iron pipe
optionD: A failure of the water meter register
sourceReference: Supporting topic reference: Corrosion in Distribution Awareness. See README for source scope and limitations.

question: What is tuberculation in a cast iron main?
correctAnswer: A buildup of rough corrosion deposits that narrows the pipe and raises friction loss
explanation: Tuberculation is the rough, mound like corrosion buildup inside iron pipe, and it reduces capacity while increasing head loss.
options: A smooth factory lining applied to new pipe
A type of valve used on large mains
A bacterial colony that only grows in reservoirs
A buildup of rough corrosion deposits that narrows the pipe and raises friction loss
optionA: A smooth factory lining applied to new pipe
optionB: A type of valve used on large mains
optionC: A bacterial colony that only grows in reservoirs
optionD: A buildup of rough corrosion deposits that narrows the pipe and raises friction loss
sourceReference: Supporting topic reference: Corrosion in Distribution Awareness. See README for source scope and limitations.

question: Which water characteristic tends to make water more corrosive to metal pipe?
correctAnswer: Low pH
explanation: Low pH water is more aggressive to metals, while stable, slightly alkaline water with adequate alkalinity tends to form protective scale instead.
options: Low pH
High alkalinity with stable pH
A stable, slightly alkaline pH
Water that has formed a protective scale
optionA: Low pH
optionB: High alkalinity with stable pH
optionC: A stable, slightly alkaline pH
optionD: Water that has formed a protective scale
sourceReference: Supporting topic reference: Corrosion in Distribution Awareness. See README for source scope and limitations.

question: Why does corrosion control matter for lead and copper at customer taps?
correctAnswer: Corrosive water can dissolve lead and copper from plumbing into drinking water
explanation: Aggressive water leaches metals from service lines, solder, and fixtures, so controlling corrosivity limits lead and copper at the tap.
options: Corrosion makes lead pipes stronger over time
Lead and copper cannot enter water from plumbing
Corrosive water can dissolve lead and copper from plumbing into drinking water
Corrosion only affects the outside of buried pipe
optionA: Corrosion makes lead pipes stronger over time
optionB: Lead and copper cannot enter water from plumbing
optionC: Corrosive water can dissolve lead and copper from plumbing into drinking water
optionD: Corrosion only affects the outside of buried pipe
sourceReference: Supporting topic reference: Corrosion in Distribution Awareness. See README for source scope and limitations.

question: A galvanic corrosion cell in a distribution system most often forms where:
correctAnswer: Two dissimilar metals are in contact in the presence of water
explanation: Galvanic corrosion needs dissimilar metals in electrical contact with an electrolyte such as water, and the less noble metal corrodes preferentially.
options: Two identical plastic pipes are joined together
A valve is left fully open for a long period
Water flows at a steady, moderate velocity
Two dissimilar metals are in contact in the presence of water
optionA: Two identical plastic pipes are joined together
optionB: A valve is left fully open for a long period
optionC: Water flows at a steady, moderate velocity
optionD: Two dissimilar metals are in contact in the presence of water
sourceReference: Supporting topic reference: Corrosion in Distribution Awareness. See README for source scope and limitations.

question: A pump trips suddenly at a booster station and a loud bang is heard in the discharge line. What phenomenon is the crew most likely dealing with?
correctAnswer: A pressure transient, or water hammer, from the sudden stop in flow
explanation: A sudden change in velocity converts kinetic energy into a pressure wave, which is water hammer and can produce the bang and damaging pressure spikes.
options: A pressure transient, or water hammer, from the sudden stop in flow
Normal cavitation at the pump eye during startup
A slow leak developing at a flange joint
Thermal expansion of water in the reservoir
optionA: A pressure transient, or water hammer, from the sudden stop in flow
optionB: Normal cavitation at the pump eye during startup
optionC: A slow leak developing at a flange joint
optionD: Thermal expansion of water in the reservoir
sourceReference: Supporting topic reference: Pressure Transient Awareness. See README for source scope and limitations.

question: Which operating practice best reduces the risk of damaging transients when closing a large valve?
correctAnswer: Closing the valve slowly over a controlled period
explanation: Slow, controlled valve operation limits the rate of velocity change, which keeps the resulting pressure surge smaller.
options: Closing the valve as fast as possible
Closing the valve slowly over a controlled period
Closing the valve only during peak demand
Opening a hydrant fully at the same moment
optionA: Closing the valve as fast as possible
optionB: Closing the valve slowly over a controlled period
optionC: Closing the valve only during peak demand
optionD: Opening a hydrant fully at the same moment
sourceReference: Supporting topic reference: Pressure Transient Awareness. See README for source scope and limitations.

question: A transient pressure drop pulls pressure below atmospheric in part of a zone. Why is that a water quality concern?
correctAnswer: Contaminated groundwater or soil water can be drawn in through leaks or submerged air valves
explanation: Negative pressure can intrude outside water through joints, leaks, or air valve openings, carrying contaminants into the main.
options: Low pressure dissolves pipe scale instantly
Negative pressure sterilizes the main interior
It only affects meter accuracy, not water quality
Contaminated groundwater or soil water can be drawn in through leaks or submerged air valves
optionA: Low pressure dissolves pipe scale instantly
optionB: Negative pressure sterilizes the main interior
optionC: It only affects meter accuracy, not water quality
optionD: Contaminated groundwater or soil water can be drawn in through leaks or submerged air valves
sourceReference: Supporting topic reference: Pressure Transient Awareness. See README for source scope and limitations.

question: Which device is commonly installed to absorb pressure surges in a pumped system?
correctAnswer: A surge tank or hydropneumatic surge vessel
explanation: Surge vessels give the pressure wave somewhere to go, absorbing energy and limiting peak and minimum pressures.
options: A surge tank or hydropneumatic surge vessel
A larger check valve with a heavier disc
A second pressure reducing valve set lower
A magnetic flow meter on the suction line
optionA: A surge tank or hydropneumatic surge vessel
optionB: A larger check valve with a heavier disc
optionC: A second pressure reducing valve set lower
optionD: A magnetic flow meter on the suction line
sourceReference: Supporting topic reference: Pressure Transient Awareness. See README for source scope and limitations.

question: After a major transient event, what is the most appropriate first field response?
correctAnswer: Inspect the affected mains, valves, and appurtenances for damage and check pressures before returning to normal operation
explanation: Transients can crack pipe, displace joints, and damage valves, so the affected section is inspected and pressures are verified before normal operation resumes.
options: Ignore it if water is still flowing
Inspect the affected mains, valves, and appurtenances for damage and check pressures before returning to normal operation
Raise the zone pressure well above normal to test the pipe
Flush every hydrant in the system at once
optionA: Ignore it if water is still flowing
optionB: Inspect the affected mains, valves, and appurtenances for damage and check pressures before returning to normal operation
optionC: Raise the zone pressure well above normal to test the pipe
optionD: Flush every hydrant in the system at once
sourceReference: Supporting topic reference: Pressure Transient Awareness. See README for source scope and limitations.

question: A certified Class 2 operator in charge of a distribution system discovers a result that could indicate a health related concern. What is the operator duty under provincial drinking water requirements in general terms?
correctAnswer: Report the concern promptly through the required notification chain and follow the system response procedures
explanation: Provincial requirements expect timely reporting of adverse or concerning results through the designated chain, so corrective action and public health protection are not delayed.
options: Wait until the next scheduled monthly report to mention it
Discuss it only with other operators and take no further action
Report the concern promptly through the required notification chain and follow the system response procedures
Post the result on social media so the public hears first
optionA: Wait until the next scheduled monthly report to mention it
optionB: Discuss it only with other operators and take no further action
optionC: Report the concern promptly through the required notification chain and follow the system response procedures
optionD: Post the result on social media so the public hears first
sourceReference: Supporting topic reference: Class 2 Operator Duties. See README for source scope and limitations.

question: Which record keeping duty is central to a Class 2 operator in charge?
correctAnswer: Keeping complete, accurate operating records, including monitoring results, maintenance, and corrective actions
explanation: Complete records demonstrate that monitoring and corrective actions actually happened, and they are the evidence reviewers and regulators rely on.
options: Keeping complete, accurate operating records, including monitoring results, maintenance, and corrective actions
Keeping records only for days when a problem occurred
Letting each operator keep private notes with no central file
Recording only the final monthly averages

question: An uncertified helper is available on a busy day. Which assignment respects certification duties in general terms?
correctAnswer: The helper works only under the direction of a certified operator and does not independently make operating decisions that require certification

The helper signs off on monitoring records alone
The helper works only under the direction of a certified operator and does not independently make operating decisions that require certification
The helper adjusts treatment related settings without supervision

correctAnswer: The plan sets the locations, frequency, and parameters needed to show the water meets provincial requirements

The plan sets the locations, frequency, and parameters needed to show the water meets provincial requirements
Sampling is optional when the water looks clear
The plan exists only for the laboratory scheduling

question: A neighbouring system asks who is designated as operator in charge during a vacation absence. What should be in place?
correctAnswer: A qualified, certified operator formally designated to act as operator in charge during the absence
explanation: An operator in charge must be designated and hold appropriate certification at all times, including during absences, so accountability never lapses.
options: No designation, because the system runs itself
The most senior labourer, regardless of certification
A rotating duty shared by all staff including uncertified staff
A qualified, certified operator formally designated to act as operator in charge during the absence

question: A customer reports a chemical taste that began this morning, and two neighbours on the same street report the same taste. What is the best interpretation for the investigator?
correctAnswer: A localized system cause is likely, so the street and nearby mains should be investigated, not just the one house
explanation: Matching complaints from several homes on one street point to a shared distribution cause, so the investigation widens to that section of main.
options: It is certainly a problem inside the first customer plumbing
A localized system cause is likely, so the street and nearby mains should be investigated, not just the one house
Complaints from neighbours can be ignored as coincidence
The whole reservoir should be drained immediately

A need to replace the entire street main at once
A localized disturbance or a short section of affected water, rather than a system wide quality failure

correctAnswer: Location, time it was noticed, description of the taste or odour, and whether neighbours are affected

question: A single home has low pressure while all neighbours have normal pressure. Where should the investigation focus first?
correctAnswer: The service line, meter, and household plumbing for that home
explanation: When only one service is affected and the surrounding main performs normally, the cause is almost always between the main and the taps in that home.

The reservoir outlet main
The pressure zone boundary valves for the whole town

question: After resolving a complaint, why does the operator call the customer back with the findings?
correctAnswer: Closing the loop confirms the problem is resolved and preserves trust and the complaint record
explanation: A follow up confirms the fix worked at the tap, completes the record, and shows the customer the concern was taken seriously.

question: When a new service connection is installed, why is the tap usually made while the main is under pressure where the procedure allows it?
correctAnswer: A wet tap avoids shutting down the main and interrupting customers
explanation: Tapping under pressure keeps the main in service, avoids a shutdown and depressurization, and reduces the contamination risk that comes with opening the main.
options: A wet tap avoids shutting down the main and interrupting customers
Pressure makes the pipe easier to cut by hand
A dry main would be too light to work on
It removes the need for a corporation stop

question: What is the purpose of the curb stop on a service line?
correctAnswer: To shut off water to the property from the street side without entering the home
explanation: The curb stop at or near the property line lets the utility isolate that service for repairs or emergencies from outside the building.
options: To measure the volume used by the customer
To boost pressure to upper floors
To vent air from the main
To shut off water to the property from the street side without entering the home

question: A service line leaks on the section between the curb stop and the house. In most program frameworks, whose repair responsibility is that section typically?
correctAnswer: The property owner, while the utility is responsible for the section from the main to the curb stop
explanation: Responsibility is commonly split at the curb stop, with the utility owning the street side and the owner responsible for the building side, subject to local bylaws.

The property owner, while the utility is responsible for the section from the main to the curb stop
The neighbouring property owner
No one, because that section cannot leak

question: Why do service connection programs require an approved backflow preventer on higher hazard commercial services?
correctAnswer: To stop contaminated water in the customer system from flowing back into the public main
explanation: A backflow preventer protects the public system from reverse flow at the connection, which is the core of cross connection control at services.
options: To increase the customer water pressure
To reduce the customer metered volume
To keep the service line from freezing
To stop contaminated water in the customer system from flowing back into the public main

optionB: To reduce the customer metered volume

question: Before excavating to install a new service, what program step protects other buried infrastructure?
correctAnswer: Obtaining locates for existing underground utilities in the work area

Obtaining locates for existing underground utilities in the work area
Ordering the meter in advance
Notifying the billing department

question: A covered reservoir shows a steadily falling chlorine residual at the outlet while inlet residual is normal, and turnover has been low for two weeks. What is the best operational response?
correctAnswer: Increase turnover by adjusting operating levels and cycling more stored water, then recheck residuals
explanation: Low turnover ages the stored water and decays residual, so cycling more water through the reservoir restores fresher water and residual at the outlet.
options: Increase turnover by adjusting operating levels and cycling more stored water, then recheck residuals
Add more water and keep the level as high and still as possible
Ignore it because the inlet residual is normal
Seal the reservoir vents to keep chlorine in

They are only decorative features on the roof
They are entry points for insects, animals, debris, and surface water that can contaminate stored water
Inspection is only needed after a flood

question: Two cells of a reservoir are available, and one cell needs internal inspection. What operating plan best protects supply and quality?
correctAnswer: Isolate and drain only the cell to be inspected while the other cell stays in service, after confirming it can carry demand

Isolate and drain only the cell to be inspected while the other cell stays in service, after confirming it can carry demand
Keep both cells online and send the inspector in with the water
Close the reservoir outlet for the whole week

question: Ice has formed across the surface of a storage facility in a cold climate. Which risk does the operator manage most directly?
correctAnswer: Damage to liners, ladders, and level instruments, and restricted venting and access

question: Level records show the reservoir repeatedly fills at night and barely draws down during the day. What system level conclusion should the operator draw?

question: A supervisor notices a pattern of small, repeated near misses around hydrant operation by several crews. What is the best use of that pattern?
correctAnswer: Treat it as a training and procedure issue, review the technique with all crews, and update the practice if the procedure itself is unclear
explanation: Repeated near misses across crews signal a system issue with training or the procedure, so the fix addresses the pattern, not just one person.
options: Discipline the last operator involved and close the matter
Treat it as a training and procedure issue, review the technique with all crews, and update the practice if the procedure itself is unclear
Wait for an actual injury before acting
Remove hydrant duties from all crews permanently
optionA: Discipline the last operator involved and close the matter
optionB: Treat it as a training and procedure issue, review the technique with all crews, and update the practice if the procedure itself is unclear
optionC: Wait for an actual injury before acting
optionD: Remove hydrant duties from all crews permanently

question: At shift handover, the outgoing operator mentions a valve that was left partly closed but does not record it. Why should the supervisor insist it be logged and communicated?
correctAnswer: An unrecorded valve position can cause low pressure, poor fire flow, and wasted troubleshooting for the next crew
explanation: Valve status is operating information the whole team depends on, so it must be recorded and handed over, not carried as one person memory.
options: Valve positions do not affect system operation
Logging it would slow the handover too much
An unrecorded valve position can cause low pressure, poor fire flow, and wasted troubleshooting for the next crew
Only the operator who moved it needs to know
optionA: Valve positions do not affect system operation
optionB: Logging it would slow the handover too much
optionC: An unrecorded valve position can cause low pressure, poor fire flow, and wasted troubleshooting for the next crew
optionD: Only the operator who moved it needs to know
